title: Delinquency Stages on Personal Credit Cards: Counting, Suspension and Charge-Off
content:
Days past due on a card under Personal Credit Cards count calendar days since the earliest due date whose minimum payment remains unpaid, and reset to zero when all past-due minimums are paid.

| Stage | What the records must show | What follows |
|---|---|---|
| Suspension | days past due reaches the tier's suspension milestone | Charging privileges are suspended |
| Restoration | days past due returns to zero on a suspended account | The account is restored to active |
| Charge-off | days past due reaches the tier's charge-off milestone | The balance is charged off, which forfeits all rewards points |

Charging privileges are suspended when days past due reaches the tier's suspension milestone, and the account's status is read from the bank's own card record. A suspended account is restored to active when days past due returns to zero. The balance is charged off when days past due reaches the tier's charge-off milestone, which forfeits all rewards points; the balance remains owed and passes to recovery outside this charter.

Payment arrangements, settlements and hardship programs for delinquent balances are outside this policy.

*On the counting.* Where two minimum payments stand unpaid, the count runs from the earlier of the two due dates, not the later. Where every past-due minimum is paid, the count is zero again, and a suspended account is restored on that footing.
